The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees that if a function \( f \) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \( N \) lies between \( f(a) \) and \( f(b) \), then there exists some \( c \) in \([a, b]\) such that \( f(c) = N \) [1].

From the right, \( x+2 \) is still positive, so the denominator stays positive, and the overall fraction remains large and negative. Thus, both sides approach \( -\infty \).

The sign stays the same on both sides of \( x = 1 \) because \( (x-1)^2 \) is always positive, and \( x+2 \) remains positive near \( x = 1 \). This makes the denominator always positive, so the negative numerator determines the sign of the whole expression [1].
